item.title: Healthy Food and Sustainable Consumption: What Do We Know and Where to Next?
item.content:encoded:
Natalina Zlatevska, University of Technology Sydney

Aya Aboelenien, HEC Montréal

Søren Askegaard, University of Southern Denmark

Belinda Barton, Bond University

Liisa Lähteenmäki, Aarhus University

Carolina Werle, Grenoble Ecole de Management

Food consumption intersects with critical challenges including diet-related health issues, environmental sustainability, and inequality. Marketing influences consumer choices through information, pricing, interventions, and cultural meanings. Research has examined approaches like labelling, nudges, and reformulation, but these studies have developed separately across disciplines, leaving gaps in understanding how interventions interact and scale.

This special issue integrates perspectives from consumer behaviour, public health, economics, and sustainability to develop a comprehensive understanding of how marketing can support healthier and more sustainable food systems. It emphasizes the broader systems in which consumption occurs, including families, social networks, cultural practices, firms, policy structures, and value chains.

The issue welcomes empirical and conceptual research, reviews, and meta-analyses that bridge theory with practical implications for policy, industry, and society. Priority is given to interdisciplinary work examining intervention effectiveness, government policy, labelling, product reformulation, consumer adaptation, equity, and structural barriers.

Appel publié par European Journal of Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Nudges and behavioural interventions for healthy and sustainable food consumption
  • Government policies and regulatory interventions
  • Food labelling and information disclosure
  • Product reformulation and industry responses
  • Trade-offs between health and environmental sustainability
  • Equity, access and unintended consequences
  • Consumer resistance and long-term behaviour change
  • Family influence and intergenerational food practices
  • Food consumption in households, communities and social networks
  • Food value chains and structural barriers
  • Consumer culture and food-related practices
  • Marketplace ideologies and cultural politics of health and sustainability

Timeline

  • February 28, 2027: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • April 30, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Alternative Proteins for Sustainable and Ethical Food Systems: Consumer, Production, and Supply-Chain Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Sina Ahmadi Kaliji, Università di Bologna

Margo Degieter, Ghent University

Hans De Steur, Ghent University

Luca Camanzi, Università di Bologna

Marleen Onwezen, Wageningen University and Research

The global food system faces mounting pressures from climate change, biodiversity loss, and sustainability concerns. Alternative proteins such as cultured meat, plant-based options, insect-based products, and novel dairy substitutes offer potential solutions. However, understanding how these alternatives reshape the broader food system remains incomplete, as existing research often examines consumption, production, and regulation in isolation without addressing value-chain restructuring, producer adoption, and governance.

This special issue seeks integrated research bridging consumer perspectives with production and supply-chain dynamics, addressing how individual decisions interact with system-level factors like regulations and policies. Contributions should explore producer decision-making, market development, environmental and animal-welfare implications, regulatory environments, and economic feasibility of alternative protein systems. The collection aims to generate actionable insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders navigating sustainable protein transitions.

Appel publié par British Food Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer acceptance and willingness to pay for alternative proteins
  • Farm-level decision-making and economic feasibility
  • Sustainability and life-cycle assessments of alternative protein supply chains
  • Regulatory frameworks, certification and labelling
  • Cultural, ethical and societal narratives
  • Communication and trust-building strategies
  • Cultured meat production systems
  • Plant-based meat analogues
  • Insect-based foods and products
  • Alternative dairy products
  • Animal welfare implications
  • Supply-chain coordination and value-chain restructuring
  • Rural livelihoods and producer adoption
  • Market development and price formation
  • Individual versus system-level dynamics
  • Policy implications for protein transitions

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions
